Change nothing else in those files, and do not touch .claude/.

entries.note: The datasource now uses one set of variables from end to end: DB_NAME, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD and DB_PORT, read by application.yml and by the database service in docker-compose.yml alike, with the same defaults on both sides. The database and user default to the artifact name ("-" becomes "_"). The password has no default anywhere: it lives in an untracked .env that docker compose reads and application.yml imports (spring.config.import: optional:file:.env[.properties]). Every database and Kafka host port is a variable. Projects generated before this change default application.yml to one database and user while the postgres service creates appdb/app/app, so the run on the host fails to log in even with the container healthy, and the compose password default contradicts .claude/rules/secrets.md. `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java compose` and /arch-doctor now print that disagreement as a warning. It never blocks, and nothing breaks if you keep the old wiring and it works for you.
entries.prompt: Bring this project's datasource wiring to the convention in .claude/skills/docker-architect/SKILL.md steps 4.5 and 5, .claude/skills/docker-architect/templates/postgres-service.yml.example (or mysql-service.yml.example) and .claude/skills/docker-architect/templates/env.example.example. First, if docker-compose.yml has no postgres or mysql service, say so and stop. Pick ONE database name and ONE user: the ones the running database already has, if its volume holds data you want to keep (docker exec <container> env shows only what the container was started with, so list the databases and roles from inside the database); otherwise the artifact name with - replaced by _. In docker-compose.yml: the database service reads POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_NAME:-<name>}, POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-<user>}, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:?set DB_PASSWORD in .env} (MYSQL_* likewise, MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD from DB_ROOT_PASSWORD), publishes "${DB_PORT:-<port>}:<port>", and its healthcheck reads $${POSTGRES_USER} and $${POSTGRES_DB}. The app service sets DB_URL (compose hostname, ${DB_NAME:-<name>}), DB_USERNAME and DB_PASSWORD by those names, replacing any SPRING_DATASOURCE_* entry. If Kafka is there, its host ports become ${KAFKA_PORT:-9092} and ${KAFKA_EXTERNAL_PORT:-29092}, the EXTERNAL advertised listener reads the same variable, and spring.kafka.bootstrap-servers defaults to localhost:${KAFKA_EXTERNAL_PORT:29092}. In application.yml: spring.config.import: optional:file:.env[.properties] (multi-module: optional:file:../.env[.properties],optional:file:.env[.properties]), url ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:${DB_PORT:<port>}/${DB_NAME:<name>}}, username ${DB_USERNAME:<user>}, password ${DB_PASSWORD} with no default. Rename any ${DB_USER} to ${DB_USERNAME}. Create .env.example with the keys and empty values, and add .env to .gitignore and .dockerignore. Write .env only if it does not exist: DB_PASSWORD is the password the database volume already uses when you keep the data (ask me for it, never guess it, never print it), or a random one otherwise. Never read .env back into the conversation. If you changed the name, user or password of a database whose volume already holds data, tell me that the image applies them only to an empty volume and that docker compose down -v applies them by deleting the data, and do not run it. Then run java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java compose, show me its output, and run the build's verify goal.

entries.note: The 'integration tests actually ran' step of .github/workflows/build.yml had two defects. First, it failed builds where every integration test passed: with Maven, as soon as one IT holds its tests in @Nested classes (failsafe writes Tests run: 0 in the enclosing class's .txt report); with Gradle, when @Nested ITs are the only ITs (every report is named <Outer>$<Nested>.xml, which *IT.xml does not match). Second, it never caught the Docker guard it exists for: a class switched off by @EnabledIf is reported as skipped, not as zero tests, so the step stayed green. The step now sums the build tool's aggregate counts and fails when any integration test was skipped or none ran (.claude/rules/testing.md § Database in integration tests). /arch-adopt does not write .github/workflows/, so a project generated before this change keeps the old step. Once fixed, an IT with @Disabled or a failed assumption also fails CI.
entries.prompt: Rewrite the 'integration tests actually ran' step of .github/workflows/build.yml to follow .claude/rules/testing.md § Database in integration tests. Keep its first part as it is: no *IT.java under any src/test/java means exit 0 with an informational line. Replace everything after it. With Maven, find every */target/failsafe-reports/failsafe-summary.xml (one per module); none means exit 1, failsafe is not wired up. Sum <completed> and <skipped> over all of them; completed already includes skipped. With Gradle, find every XML under */build/test-results/integrationTest/, whatever its name ends with, since @Nested reports are named <Outer>$<Nested>.xml; none means exit 1. Sum the tests and skipped attributes of each file's <testsuite> element. In both cases, skipped > 0 means exit 1: print the count and the class of every report whose <testsuite> has a non-zero skipped attribute. A total of zero means exit 1. Otherwise print how many ran. The step runs under bash -eo pipefail, so a grep or find that may match nothing must not end the script. Read no per-class .txt report. Before changing anything, list every IT under src/test/java that carries @Disabled or an assumption, because each one will fail CI after this change, and wait for my go-ahead.

Once changed, a project that already has one of those lines red goes red in CI.
entries.prompt: In .github/workflows/build.yml, in the job named 'architectural boundaries', change the step that runs `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor` so it runs `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor gate`. Replace the comment above it with: '# Fails when a committed check of the .claude/ setup is red — the lines doctor.gate.labels names in .claude/schemas/extensions.json. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and Compose are runner state and never gate.' Change nothing else. Before committing, run `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor gate` locally and show me its last lines; if it exits 1, list the failing lines and wait for my go-ahead.

entries.note: An approved spec is now implemented by `/new-feature-implement UC-NNN-slug`, a skill of its own. `/new-feature` only designs: over an approved case it stops and prints the `/clear` and `/new-feature-implement` lines instead of implementing. Nothing in src/ changes. One project setting can be left behind: an audit opt-out in .claude/audit-usage/audited.json is matched by piece name, so a project that switched `new-feature` off keeps auditing implement runs until it names the new skill too.
entries.prompt: Check .claude/audit-usage/audited.json. If the file does not exist, or its `skills` object does not set `new-feature`, tell me there is nothing to do and stop. Otherwise add `"new-feature-implement"` to `skills` with the same boolean `new-feature` has, change nothing else in the file, and show me the diff.

entries.note: SonarQube now measures coverage over the same classes as the build's JaCoCo gate. .claude/rules/testing.md § Coverage leaves the startup class and the configuration classes out, and the root build file's JaCoCo excludes do that. Sonar does not read those excludes, so before this change it reported those classes as uncovered. sonarqube-setup now writes sonar.coverage.exclusions, derived from the JaCoCo excludes in the root build file. It configures a project once and never runs again on a project that already has the scanner, and /arch-adopt writes no build file. So a project set up with Sonar before this change keeps the wider scope until it adds the property. Only matters if the root build file has the SonarQube scanner.
entries.prompt: Make this project's SonarQube coverage scope match its JaCoCo gate, as .claude/skills/sonarqube-setup/SKILL.md step 3 now describes. First, if the root pom.xml has no sonar-maven-plugin (Gradle: the root build.gradle has no org.sonarqube plugin), tell me there is nothing to do and stop. Otherwise read the JaCoCo excludes of the root build file: with Maven, the <excludes> in the <configuration> of jacoco-maven-plugin; with Gradle, the exclude: list of jacocoTestReport's classDirectories. If there are none, tell me so and stop. Turn each trailing .class into .java, keep directory patterns such as **/config/** unchanged, and join them with commas in their order. Show me the line you will add and wait for my go-ahead. With Maven, add <sonar.coverage.exclusions>…</sonar.coverage.exclusions> next to the other sonar.* entries in the root pom.xml's <properties>. With Gradle, add property 'sonar.coverage.exclusions', '…' inside the root sonar { properties { } } block. Do not set sonar.exclusions, and change nothing else. entries.note: Projects are now generated with agent instruction files that agents other than Claude Code read. Each module with import restrictions has an AGENTS.md that owns its facts, and next to it a CLAUDE.md holding only `@AGENTS.md`, which is how Claude Code loads it — GitHub Copilot reads a module AGENTS.md and never a module CLAUDE.md. entries.prompt: Add this project's agent instruction files, as Nerviz's project-bootstrap step 6 now writes them. entries.note: The CI job `architectural boundaries` now fails on a forbidden import, whoever wrote it. `doctor gate` gained a `Boundary violations` line that sweeps every source file against .claude/forbidden-imports.txt — the same match the edit-time `check` hook applies — where before it only counted the rules, and nothing refused an import written outside Claude Code until the ArchUnit test was installed. A project that already carries such an import goes red on its next push. Run `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor` to see them before you push.
entries.prompt: Fix every forbidden import that `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor` lists under its `Boundary violations` line. For each file named there, the import is forbidden in that module by .claude/forbidden-imports.txt, generated from the blueprint and enforced as .claude/rules/architecture-ddd.md describes: move the code that needs the framework type to the module that may depend on it — usually an adapter, or the configuration of the module that holds the main class — and leave in the restricted module only what it is allowed to know, behind a port if the use case needs it. Never edit .claude/forbidden-imports.txt to make the line pass. Change one module at a time, run the build after each, and finish with `java .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java doctor gate`, which must exit 0.

entries.note: Three sentences a single-module project may carry are now false or never applied. hook_build.$comment: How `ArchHook.java build` turns the source into the jar every hook registration launches, and what `schema` and `doctor` compare to call it stale. `javac_feature` is the pin: `build` refuses under any other JDK feature release, because `--verify` (run by CI) recompiles and compares class bytes, and two javac majors emit different bytes for the same source. `release` is what the classes target — the stated JDK 21+ dependency. `hash_entry` holds the SHA-256 of the source with CRLF normalized to LF: `* text=auto` gives a Windows checkout CRLF, and a raw hash would call a fresh jar stale. Design: .claude/decisions/0075-precompiled-hook-jar.md

export.$comment: Single owner of WHAT the `export` mode writes into a target project and HOW each piece is transformed. Read by ArchHook.java `export`; cross-checked by `schema` at sweep time, the same way `guard.executor_agents` is. The failure it exists to close is silent in both directions: a skill added to this repo and forgotten here never reaches any project generated afterwards, and an entry left behind after a rename points at a file that no longer exists — neither breaks anything at generation time, only for whoever reads the dead citation inside the project. That is why `include` and `exclude` together must cover every skill and every agent on disk: not listing one is the bug, and `schema` says so by name. Prose counterpart, which branch `feat/bootstrap-invokes-export` replaces with a call to the mode: project-bootstrap/SKILL.md §§ 6.6, 6.7, 6.8, 7. Design: .claude/decisions/0054-deterministic-export-provenance-plugin.md

copy.$comment: `verbatim`: copied byte for byte, skipping `transform`. The jar below carries the SHA-256 of THIS source, and `schema` compares the two inside the generated project too — a citation cut here would make every exported jar read as stale. Design: .claude/decisions/0075-precompiled-hook-jar.md

Apache License 2.0 § 4 obliges whoever redistributes the work to hand over the license text and the NOTICE; what `export` writes under `.claude/` is a redistribution. They sit INSIDE `.claude/`, never at the project root: the root `LICENSE` of a generated project is its owner's choice. Design: .claude/decisions/0181-apache-2-license-notice-and-trademark.md

export.$comment_binary: Copied as bytes, never read as text, never transformed. What every hook registration launches (`java -jar`), so a project that lacked it would have every hook exit 1 — which does not block. Design: .claude/decisions/0075-precompiled-hook-jar.md

overwrite.$comment: Not a merge, on purpose: re-serializing the file would reorder its keys and drop its comments, and a real three-way merge is a program nobody asked for. The export refuses a dirty worktree, so the destination's previous content is one `git diff` away and one `git checkout` from coming back. A project that added hook entries of its own loses them here and sees exactly that in the diff.

export.$comment_marker: The cross-check `schema` runs over this block only makes sense in the repository the block describes. `source_marker` is how the mode tells: a directory that exists here and travels nowhere. Without it the check fires in a throwaway tree that merely copied extensions.json — the CI injection sandbox is one — and reports every rule and skill as missing when what is actually missing is the repository.
export.$comment_blueprint: The active blueprint travels with the project, the catalog does not. Without this the yaml that defines a project's architecture can live only in the fetched tree, which is a temporary directory: the stamp records the id, the next update reads that id, the source does not have it, and the export fails at a point where nobody was ever told to keep a file (lessons-learned-011 § 4). Copied for every blueprint, official or not, because at this layer the mode cannot tell one from the other — the fetched tree holds both by then. `{id}` is the blueprint's id.
export.$comment_retired: Paths this repo renamed or dropped, deleted from the target by `export` when present (`--dry-run` names them). Export only ever wrote, so a renamed rule's old copy stayed in every adopted project — the same norm in two files there, the old one loading at launch. Restricted to .claude/; the target's worktree is clean before an export, so a deletion is one `git checkout` from undone. `schema` fails on an entry that still exists here. Files, not directories: `export` deletes regular files only, so a renamed skill lists every file it had — its now-empty directory is left behind, invisible to git and to the runtime (no SKILL.md). Design: .claude/decisions/0082-rules-without-paths-load-at-launch.md, .claude/decisions/0088-rename-java-patterns-to-gof-design-patterns.md
export.$comment_gitignore: Two lines, opposite decisions, both deliberate. `.claude/audit-usage/` itself is VERSIONED — `history.jsonl`, `nodes.jsonl` and each report belong to the commit of the run that produced them, and `git-publish` stages that directory by default; only the hook's scratch state under `.state/` is ignored. `docs/lessons-learned/` is NOT versioned: those are local notes taken while running the pipeline, not project documentation, and a run that recreates a deleted one writes different text nobody compares. Oscillating between the two is what makes every later diff start dirty — lessons-learned-012 § 15 and § 16.

rules.$comment: Every rule travels; `exclude` is empty on purpose and an entry added to it needs a reason in the commit. `00-index.md` is listed in `body_transforms.rewrite` because its paragraph about architecture_paths cites blueprints/, which the project does not have.

skills.$comment: `keep` is what travels out of each skill directory, and it is a keep-list rather than an exclude-list so that a new subdirectory here (use-case-design/examples/ was the first) stays out by default instead of leaking into every project. `exclude` holds the creation skills: they only serve before the project exists, and inside one they invite the model to regenerate on top of live code.

derived_paths.$comment_exempt: Globs that are valid in any architecture and so need no derivation: they name no package. A rule whose `paths` holds only these is not expected here. Java is `**/src/**/*.java`, never `**/*.java`, which also matches .claude/hooks/ArchHook.java and loads every Java norm on each read of the hook (0082). One that names a package and is missing from this map would travel with the glob of whichever blueprint happened to be written into the file — gap 8 of lessons-learned-001. `schema` checks both directions.
derived_paths.$comment: A rule with a territory auto-loads by `paths`, and a glob naming a package the active blueprint does not use leaves it silently unloaded. The glob is therefore derived from the blueprint's packages.map — the VALUE, not the key, with `.` becoming `/` — and never copied from the original file. `suffix` selects the packages.map entry whose key ends with it; `key` names candidates in order of preference, first hit wins. A selector that matches nothing and is `optional` keeps the master example globs, inert in that architecture — never strips them, since a rule without `paths` loads at launch in every session (.claude/decisions/0082-rules-without-paths-load-at-launch.md); one that matches nothing and is not optional is a failure of the export, not of the project. No defensive union: this blueprint's glob and no other.

authorization.md.$comment: Wiring lives in the `.config` package; hexagonal, onion and custom-template have none, so it lives in a `security` subpackage of the REST adapter and the `.rest` glob already covers it. vertical-slice has `.config` and no `.rest`, so the fallback never fires there and the rule loads on `config/**` only — a slice's controller does not pull it, and the executor cites it inline anyway (decision 0112). `.graphql` too: a GraphQL resolver carries the method-security check on every operation and sensitive field, since the filter chain sees one endpoint (decision 0146).

blueprint.$comment: Where the mode reads the architecture from, and how. `vocabulary_anchor_key` names the top-level YAML key the naming-convention comment block sits immediately above — the block is a comment in every blueprint written so far, so it is located by position rather than by a marker, and the position is data because a blueprint that moves it would otherwise need Java changed. Invariant 7: adding an architecture edits no code.

body_transforms.$comment: Applied to every copied text file. A citation to decisions/ has no counterpart inside a project, so it is cut, not rewritten: a sentence that exists only to cite the record goes whole (that is what `sentence_lead_ins` recognizes), and a citation inside a sentence that says something else loses only the citing clause. Whatever survives both is reported by `residue_markers` at the end of the run — a dead path that ships in silence is the failure this whole block exists against, and the report is what makes it not silent.
body_transforms.$comment_replacement: What neither `cut_shapes` nor `sentence_lead_ins` recognizes is a citation inside a sentence that says something else. Deleting the path there leaves the sentence mangled — `- **** —`, `Inherits D15 —.` — and no `residue_markers` entry looking for a path can see what removing the path left behind, so six of them shipped into every exported tree (lessons-learned-012 § 3). The path becomes prose instead: a reader inside a project cannot follow it either way, and the sentence still says what it was written to say. The three shape markers below are the net for the next sentence this does not cover.
body_transforms.citation_replacement: a decision recorded in the meta-repository
body_transforms.$comment_exempt: Two files name these directories on purpose and are not dead paths. `ArchHook.java`'s `export` mode prints them in its own usage and errors, and that mode refuses to run inside a project anyway (no `export` block there). `arch-adopt` talks about the tree it FETCHES, under /tmp, where blueprints/ does exist — cutting those sentences would delete the instructions instead of a citation.
body_transforms.$comment_replace: Literal find/with pairs applied to every copied file. Empty on purpose: the two pairs that lived here rewrote "the active blueprint's `packages.map`" into a pointer at the root `CLAUDE.md`, on the premise that no blueprint exists inside a project — false since `blueprint_copy` ships the active one, and the literal match missed every wrapped occurrence, so one exported skill cited two sources (lessons-learned-016 § 3). Design: .claude/decisions/0093-lessons-learned-016-fact-sources.md

mods.$comment: Single owner of what a mod of this repository may be. A mod is a plugin whose hooks/hooks.json names a hooks module: TypeScript that runs inside the Claude Code process and draws in the interface. Read by ArchHook.java `schema` (the structure of every mod under `root`, at Stop and after an edit there), `guard status` (`deny_markers`, handed to the mod with the open phase) and `doctor` (the `Mods` line, against `min_version`). A mod renders what the rest of this file already enforces through settings hooks: it holds no rule (invariant 2 — the rule stays in ArchHook.java, which the mod calls) and it is never the guarantee (invariant 6 — a mod does not load in `claude -p`, VS Code, a cloud session or under `--safe-mode`). Meta-repository only: the `export` block lists no mod and the generated project's settings template registers no marketplace, so the whole block is silent where `root` does not exist. Design: .claude/decisions/0131-mods-in-architect-designer.md
mods.$comment_versions: `min_version` is the first Claude Code release that loads a mod outside early access; `doctor` reports a lower CLI. `ci_version` is the CLI the `mods` job of .github/workflows/templates.yml installs to run `claude plugin validate` and `claude plugin test` — pinned, so a release that changes the mods API fails a pull request that raises it, not an unrelated one.
mods.$comment_events: Every event a hooks module may register with `on(...)`, transcribed from the `.d.ts` Claude Code writes into a loaded mod's .claude-plugin/types/ (EngineEventOf); that file wins when the two disagree. `classic.<Event>` is accepted for every name in `settings.hook_events` and `settings.hook_events_extra`. An unknown name fails `claude plugin validate` too, but only on a machine with the CLI — this list makes `schema` say it everywhere.
mods.$comment_gating: Events whose hook can change whether something runs — a tool call, a prompt, a subagent, the end of a turn. A hook on one of them ends in `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))`: a hook that throws or times out is otherwise skipped, and the handler makes the failure fall through to the settings hooks and `permissions` rules beneath — `next(e)` replays their decision once `next.called`, and runs them once when not. A mod here holds no refusal of its own, so the handler never needs one; a mod hooks these events only to show or hold what a guarantee beneath already decided, never to loosen it. `claude plugin validate` prints `gating hook without .catch` for the same defect, and the `mods` CI job fails on that line.
mods.$comment_calls: What a mod here never calls: the network, the model (it spends the person's plan), a prompt or message sent as the person, a change to the environment every later command inherits, and a file write that no tool-time guard sees. One write is admitted: `ArchHook.jar config set|unset`, the single writer of a project's own settings — it validates before it writes and refuses with nothing written, and `guard` refuses every other path to those files (0187). `process_allow` is the only program `$.process.run` may start — the first element of its argument list, as a string literal; the mod reaches the repository's rules through `java -jar .claude/hooks/ArchHook.jar`, and nothing else.
mods.$comment_markers: Fragments of the refusals `guard write` and `guard bash` print. `guard status` hands them to the cockpit mod, which holds a Bash refusal behind its dialog only when the refusal carries one of them — a refusal the person typed at a permission prompt carries none. `schema` fails when a marker no longer appears in ArchHook.java, so a reworded message cannot silently turn the dialog off.

boundary_map.$comment: Read by ArchHook.java `boundary-map`, which writes the generated project's `.claude/forbidden-imports.txt` from a blueprint. A multi-module blueprint carries `forbidden_imports` per module and the mode copies them (a trailing `..` becomes `.`); a single-module one carries only `dependency_rules.forbidden`, and the mode derives one line per (from, to) pair of `packages.map` entries, plus the `framework_roots` of the `from` name when this block lists it — architecture-ddd.md § Domain: both Jackson roots, since a guard that lists one lets the other through. A blueprint that declares `packages.module_slot` gets that first segment written as `{module}` on both sides of each derived line, and `check` matches `{module}` against any one directory, so modules created after bootstrap are covered (decision 0180). `source_root` is the single module's source folder, where the left side of every derived line starts. Design: .claude/decisions/0166-blueprint-skeleton-generated-in-ci.md
